script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sci-Fi
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

A RAIN-SOAKEN MAN, JAMES (50s), sits on an old leather couch, staring at a flickering TV screen. The room is dimly lit by the orange glow of the tube. Rain beats against the window.

Suddenly, a power surge and a BLINDING FLASH of light illuminates the room. James jumps up, startled.

JAMES
(shouting)
What the hell was that?

INT. LIVING ROOM - MOMENTS LATER

A KNOCK at the door. James hesitates then makes his way to answer it. He opens it to find his old friend, MARK (40s), wearing a trench coat and holding a small box.

MARK
(smiling)
Hey, James. Long time no see.

JAMES
(surprised)
Mark? What are you doing here?

MARK
(holding up the box)
I've brought you a gift. It's a prototype I've been working on. A new technology that can help us change the world. But I can't do it alone. I need your help.

James looks skeptically at the box.

JAMES
What is it?

MARK
(opening the box)
It's a Neural Interface. It can connect your brain to a computer, allowing you to access vast amounts of information, control technology, even communicate telepathically.

James raises an eyebrow.

JAMES
Sounds too good to be true.

MARK
(grinning)
It's not. But it does come with a risk. The technology is still in its early stages, and there are those who would stop us from changing the world for the better.

James thinks for a moment.

JAMES
Alright, Mark. I'm in.

INT. LAB - DAY

Mark and James work together in a high-tech laboratory. They connect the Neural Interface to a powerful computer.

MARK
(excitedly)
Are you ready for this, James?

JAMES
(nervously)
As ready as I'll ever be.

Mark helps James put on the Interface. They sit in front of the computer, their eyes closed. A soft beep sounds, and a moment later, the room is filled with a gentle hum.

INT. LAB - MOMENTS LATER

James and Mark open their eyes. They look at each other, amazed.

JAMES
(speaking telepathically)
It worked.

MARK
(smiling)
I told you it would.

INT. NEWSROOM - DAY

James and Mark, now wearing the Neural Interfaces, sit in the newsroom of a major television network. They use their telepathic abilities to access vast amounts of information and begin reporting on global events in real-time.

ANNOUNCER (V.O.)
(on TV)
BREAKING NEWS: Two men, believed to be scientists, have appeared in the newsroom of CNN, claiming to have access to top-secret global information.

James and Mark exchange glances, then focus their efforts on using their new abilities to expose corrupt politicians and corporations, and bring about positive change.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

James and Mark sit on the couch, their Neural Interfaces connected to a smaller, more portable computer. They work late into the night, their thoughts intertwined as they seek to make the world a better place.

JAMES
(thoughtfully)
Mark, I don't know how we'll be able to keep this up without getting caught.

MARK
(smiling)
We'll find a way. We have each other, and that's all we need.

James smiles back, feeling a sense of true friendship and connection that goes beyond words.

FADE OUT.

End screenplay.
